identity.intent: Make a single candle-formation decision feel immediately legible and authored through one native pixel grid, a strict palette, role-shaped characters, and restrained combat feedback.

principles.statement: Every runtime surface resolves on the 480x270 native grid.
principles.rationale: A single pixel density prevents generated sprites, UI, type, and effects from looking assembled from unrelated systems.

principles.statement: Formation role and unit behavior read before decorative fantasy detail.
principles.rationale: The game has one decision, so the visual hierarchy must make that decision effortless to parse.

principles.statement: Generated character and UI images remain source until extracted, normalized, palette-locked, imported, captured, and reviewed.
principles.rationale: This blocks polished source imagery from concealing an incoherent or unfinished game implementation.

principles.statement: Use short integer-aligned travel, impact, health, and result beats instead of continuous spectacle.
principles.rationale: Restrained motion keeps the formation causal chain visible throughout the eight-second battle.

color.rule: Sixteen shared runtime colors; hue always pairs with silhouette, position, text, health, or motion.

typography.rule: All interface copy is uppercase, short, and rendered without subpixel positioning.

layout.rule: One primary action and one visible formation rail; no card inventory or secondary navigation.

motion.idle: One- to three-pixel role-specific whole-frame breathing and moth drift
motion.action: Whole-pixel anticipation, squash, directional lunge, and recovery
motion.projectile: Curved five-pixel head with a four-step integer-aligned trail and delayed state impact
motion.impact: Brief hit-stop, bounded screen shake, recoil squash, role-colored burst, health change, and damage or healing callout
motion.defeat: Short rise, flatten, fade, and soot burst before removal
motion.result: Overshooting authored plaque reveal, progress flames, restrained rays, and replay pulse
motion.rule: Every motion beat communicates a real state change; no smooth subpixel drift, blur, or persistent emitter noise.

patterns.intent: Bind a guardian to a clear rear, center, or front role.
rules: Use the ward line as a directional rail.
Place the role name and its single bonus directly below the unit.
Selection changes the full slot arc and instruction copy.
examples: FRONT / GUARDS ALL remains visible behind the Red Warden during combat.

patterns.intent: Show who acted, what traveled, and what changed.
rules: Anticipate and lunge before launching an action.
Resolve health only when the curved projectile reaches its target.
Pair hit-stop and recoil with bounded particles and a health change.
Make rear Seer chain, center Chime pulse, and front Warden block visibly distinct.
avoid: Idle bob presented as complete animation
examples: Rear Seer compresses, lunges, sends a curved blue bolt, and arcs a second hit into the next living moth.
Front Warden's ward catches an incoming violet bolt with a gold BLOCK callout and linked formation pulse.

patterns.intent: Close the short encounter without leaving the visual system.
rules: Dim the battlefield but retain formation context.
Use a two-pixel gold or violet frame.
Keep replay available in the persistent footer.
examples: THE NIGHT BREAKS summarizes combo and duration above SPACE TO TRY AGAIN.

references.role: Generated character source sheet retained for provenance; never loaded by the runtime.
references.prompt: Production source sheet for a low-resolution 2D pixel-art autobattler called WICKWARD: exactly six isolated full-body units in a 3 by 2 sheet—three candle guardians (red shield warden, blue match-wand seer, gold bell healer) and three night moths (round soot moth, narrow violet needle moth, large ash moth). Authentic crisp 16-bit pixel art, limited palette, readable silhouettes, consistent scale and baseline, no text, UI, scenery, shadows, watermark, painterly rendering, gradients, or overlapping cells.

references.role: Generated six-motif ornament atlas retained for provenance; structural UI is deterministic and this source is never loaded by the runtime.
references.prompt: Production source atlas of exactly six decorative pixel-art UI motifs for Wickward: candle-flame crest, crossed ward-line knot, night-moth sigil, wax-drip edge accent, square brass corner cap, and round brass rivet. One motif per equal cell in a 3 by 2 atlas on flat chroma green, all at the same apparent pixel density and scale, using the existing Wickward palette and crisp 16-bit pixel language. Ornaments only: no complete panels, buttons, frames, health bars, text, characters, scenery, giant ornaments, mismatched pixel densities, gradients, or watermark.
